correctness.rationale: The rules agree with Jiang's Definitions 2.2–2.3. At q=0 each nonempty cut gives identity or a rotation with probability 1/2 each, and empty cuts are identity, so the base walk mixes geometrically within each orbit xH of right multiplication. With one broken internal bond the split packet is A,C and the other packet is B. Only A,B,C separates the two parts and leaves H; block-weighted release gives it probability 1/3, midpoint keys force it, and a specified break has probability w_k q(1−q)^(n−3). All other off-H effects are O_n(q²). Averaging Π over H annihilates the within-H first-order contribution on orbit-constant functions; the remaining averaged coefficients yield precisely L and 3L. For the averaging error, use an equivalent norm in which the q=0 fast block contracts by ρ<1. The slow/fast coupling is O(q); bounded powers of the full stochastic kernel give fast size O(ρ'^t+q) with ρ'<1. The accumulated slow error through t=O(q^−1) is O(q) by geometric summation and t q²=O(q). Its Euler limit is the orbit semigroup, with the fast component vanishing at each s>0. The event with cut 2 and break 1 supplies g=(2 3 … n), which with rotation r generates S_n since rg^−1=(1 2); the directed finite support generates the same group as its inverses. Left translation ensures uniform stationarity. Positive-time irreducible kernels strictly contract a nonzero zero-mass signed measure, and invertibility prevents exact finite-time stationarity. This gives a strict crossing at all stated ε and allows monotone bracketing of both discrete mixing times. The s=0 boundary layer is properly excluded. The phrase 'right-coset' describes the right-action orbit here; xH is conventionally a left coset, but the explicit formulas fix the correct convention. The supplied code was inspected, not executed, and its finite coverage would not itself prove the theorem.

value.rationale: For two natural release kernels previously compared by mixing order, this determines the exact relative clock and the entire nontrivial positive-time full-deck profile for arbitrary fixed deck size. Identifying the one-bond contribution for every cut explains why different releases give the same orbit dynamics after time change, and fixes threshold-dependent constants that the common Θ order and four-card spectrum cannot give. The conclusion neither claims a finite-adhesion time-change identity nor extrapolates to a joint large-deck limit.
